answer: Issuers publish a revocation bitmap where each credential holds one bit, and a verifier checks the bit before accepting a presentation: a revoked credential shows a set bit and is rejected even if its signature is valid. The registry updates the bitmap in a spiral of signed snapshots, so a Sybil that reuses a revoked credential is caught at the jetty of verification, unable to cross the lagoon of trust twice with the same dead pass.
